prompt.es: Escribe un relato a dos voces sobre el mismo hecho, con los recursos de la clase.

answer.text: Ana's version. I recall that night clearly. The concert was perfect: I was standing next to a food stall with a cold drink, and the music was great. Then, suddenly, the lights went out. "Stay here," Leo whispered, and he disappeared into the dark. Afterwards, he insisted that he had only wanted to help, whereas I remember only the fear. By then, the crowd had gone quiet and nobody moved. Had I followed him, I would have got lost in the park. Years later, that memory still feels bitter. Leo's version. My sister recalls the silence; however, I remember the music, which never stopped. I remember the smell of rain and the guitar, still playing in the dark. I found the cable behind the stage and fixed it in five minutes. "Why did you leave me?" she asked when I came back. "I wanted to help," I replied. If I hadn't gone, the concert would have been cancelled, and nobody would have seen the lights come back. Looking back, I understand why she was angry. Afterwards we laughed about it, but we still tell the story in two different ways.
accepted: Ana's version. I recall that night clearly. The concert was perfect: I was standing next to a food stall with a cold drink, and the music was great. Then, suddenly, the lights went out. "Stay here," Leo whispered, and he disappeared into the dark. Afterwards, he insisted that he had only wanted to help, whereas I remember only the fear. By then, the crowd had gone quiet and nobody moved. Had I followed him, I would have got lost in the park. Years later, that memory still feels bitter. Leo's version. My sister recalls the silence; however, I remember the music, which never stopped. I remember the smell of rain and the guitar, still playing in the dark. I found the cable behind the stage and fixed it in five minutes. "Why did you leave me?" she asked when I came back. "I wanted to help," I replied. If I hadn't gone, the concert would have been cancelled, and nobody would have seen the lights come back. Looking back, I understand why she was angry. Afterwards we laughed about it, but we still tell the story in two different ways.

Mia's version. I remember the platform very well. The train was late, so Tom and I waited in the cold. "Let's go home," I said, but he insisted that we stay. By then, the last bus had left. Had he listened to me, we would have been warm in bed. Afterwards, I was angry for a week. Tom's version. My friend recalls the cold, whereas I remember the moment the train finally arrived. "You were right," she whispered, when we sat down at last. If we had gone home, we would have missed the best night of the trip. Looking back, I think we were both a little right. Years later, we still argue about it, however, and we both enjoy telling the story.

answer.text: Notice to all neighbours. We apologise for the change, but the street festival has been postponed until Sunday. Tom told us that the generator had broken down, and Mrs Lopez complained that the music was too loud. We would rather postpone the festival than cancel it, as the permit only allows music until ten. Would you consider moving your stalls to the park on Sunday morning? Had the generator not broken down, the festival would have started today. Please contact the organisers if you need help. Thank you for your understanding.
